Bangalore  has all you might want, whether you're searching for a fun place to dance the evening away or a nice place to have few drinks with friends. We'll explore the city's top bars with dance floors to make sure you have an amazing time.


 Table Of Contents

", "blogcontentId": "584"}

{"content": "

Bangalore partygoers associate Big Brewsky with delicious cuisine, amazing craft beer, and of course, dancing and music. This microbrewery will give you a memorable evening thanks to its unique lighting, first-rate service, amazing menu, romantic atmosphere, and captivating d\u00e9cor. ", "blogcontentId": "591"}

{"content": "

Factors to Consider When Choosing a Pub

When selecting a pub with a dance floor in Bangalore, there are several factors to keep in mind:
Location and Accessibility
Think about where the bar is located and how convenient it is to go to from where you are starting from. For most visitors, pubs in key locations like MG Road, Brigade Road, and Koramangala are more handy.
Timings and Best Days to Visit
In Bangalore, the majority of pubs are open from late afternoon into the wee hours of the morning. The best days to go, meanwhile, could change based on the theme or special activities of the bar. For the most recent information about the pub's schedule and forthcoming events, it's a good idea to visit their website or social media accounts.
Cost Estimates and Reservation Advice
The cost of a pub varies according to geography, cuisine, and knowledge. It's a good idea to know how much you can afford before choosing a pub. Make arrangements in advance to avoid any issues, as some locations especially on weekends or during major events may need reservations.
Dress Code and Entry Requirements
The majority of pubs in Bangalore have a smart casual dress code. It's usually a good idea to find out the precise dress code and admission requirements of the bar, as some may have age restrictions or additional legal criteria.

Conclusion

Bangalore has an amazing nightlife society with many of different bars that have amazing dance floors and great memories. There is a bar out there that matches your tastes and makes sure you have a great evening. So gather your buddies, get dressed up, and prepare to have a great time dancing in one of Bangalore's best bars of the evening.

", "blogcontentId": "592"}

To break free from this cycle, you must evaluate your options independently. Think about what you really want in a home. Dive into the process with curiosity and openness.

Area: 1,200 sq. ft.

The Center's latest modifications have increased realtor shares, which has pleased the real estate sector. People can now choose to pay 12.5% in taxes without accounting for inflation or 20% in taxes with inflation adjustment if they sell their property before July 23, 2024.

Key Takeaways

  • For long-term capital gains on real estate sales, the Center modified the indexation standards. 
  • The tax rate options available to taxpayers are 12.5% without indexation and 20% with indexation.
  • Following the news, real estate stocks\u2014such as Oberoi Realty and Lodha Developers\u2014saw considerable gains.
  • Industry experts view this move as a positive step for the real estate market.
", "blogcontentId": "563"}

{"content": "

Centre's Amendment to Indexation Rules

Property owners expect to gain from the changes that the Center has suggested to the long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax regulations. For houses sold before July 23, 2024, they will now have a choice between a 12.5% tax rate without indexation and a 20% rate with indexation. This change comes after the Budget 2024 was released by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, who faced criticism for possibly raising taxes on long-term property owners by eliminating indexation advantages.Before, LTCG was subject to a 20% tax rate that was index-linked to account for inflation.

Read More:How the Removal of Indexation Benefits Affects High-End Real Estate

Impact on Realty Stocks

Shares of several real estate companies did not rise when the modification was announced. August 7, 2024 saw an approximate 1% increase in the BSE Realty index. Among the biggest gainers were Lodha Developers, Oberoi Realty, DLF.

                    Realty Company

      Stock Price Change (%)

                      Lodha Developers

                                                     2.1%

                        Oberoi Realty

                                                     2%

                                DLF

                                                     1.7%

                       Godrej Properties

                                                      0.8%

Industry Experts' Views

 Experts are happy about the Centre\u2019s new tax rule change.

 Niranjan Hiranandani, a prominent figure in the real estate sector, stated, \"The government's initiative to allow taxpayers to compute taxes at 12.5% without indexation or 20% with indexation on real estate transactions marks a significant step forward, poised to drive investment and boost housing sales.\"

Deepak Shenoy, the Founder and CEO of Capital Mind, also praised the change by saying, \"Good idea. Will help quell that drama.\"

Furthermore, Hemal Mehta from Deloitte India noted, \"This amendment gives relief to taxpayers, allowing them to choose the more beneficial regime.\"

Overall, experts believe the change will make property owners' lives easier and improve the real estate market.

The Rationale Behind the Amendment

Numerous conversations with real estate industry players provided the basis for the modification. There have been worries expressed that the new tax structure may have an adverse impact on the industry and greatly raise householders' tax bill. After taking into account the objections raised, the government decided to change the idea so that property owners could select the tax regime that best suited their budget. It is expected that this flexibility will lead to more  real estate investment, which will ultimately result in more housing sales.

Changes in Taxation Structure

The following are the changes made to the tax structure:
Under the proposed plan, taxes on properties acquired before July 23, 2024, can be calculated at 12.5% without indexation.
Under the previous plan, properties acquired before July 23, 2024, are subject to 20% tax computation with indexation.
Of the two possibilities, taxpayers can decide to pay the smaller tax. 

The Road Ahead for Real Estate

It is anticipated that the new tax reform will shortly support the real estate market. More people may choose to invest in real estate if property owners gain a better understanding of their tax obligations. Tax breaks for property owners are intended to promote increased investment and growth because real estate is crucial for the economy and employment.

Conclusion

It will be interesting to watch how the real estate market is affected by these new tax regulations. More options for property owners are provided by the new regulations, which should benefit them and attract more real estate investors.

", "blogcontentId": "564"}
blogs.excerpt: Realtor stocks rise as the Centre revises indexation rules, boosting market confidence and investment opportunities.
blogs.title: Realtor Stocks Up After Centre Revises Indexation Rules

Bengaluru, another name for Bangalore, is a vibrant city that skillfully combines technology and heritage. Some of the most well-known temples in the city, which are a reflection of its rich cultural legacy, may be found among its busy IT hubs and metropolitan settings. These temples draw tourists from all over the world not just as places of worship but also as architectural wonders.

Table of Contents

", "blogcontentId": "554"}

{"content": "

When you enter the Chokkanathaswamy Temple in Domlur, you'll be taken back in time to the tenth century. The inner sanctum and a few ardhamantapas (hallways) remain intact after decades of remodeling. You can look at the sculptures and the Tamil writings on the walls for a while.
Address: 5th Cross Road, Opposite Sony World, Village Domlur, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560071
Timings: 6AM-11AM, 5:45PM-8:30PM,6:00AM \u2013 11:30AM, 5:45PM \u2013 8:30PM (Wednesday)|6:00AM-12:30PM, 5:45PM-9:00PM (Saturday)

", "blogcontentId": "555"}

{"content": "

Dodda Basavana Gudi, located in Bugle Rock Park in Basavanagudi, is a regular feature on vacation brochures. Kempegowda, the founder of the city, constructed it in 1573. The enormous granite sculpture of Nandi, the bull demi-god, is the main draw here. A short walk away is the Dodda Ganeshana Gudi, which is equally popular. Here, worshippers swarm to obtain the blessings of a stone statue of Ganesha. This is the location of the renowned groundnut mela, or kadalekai parishe, which takes place at the end of the year. After seeing the temple, don't forget to take a look around Bugle Park. It is thought that these rock formations date back more than three million years! Lastly, a visit to Bugle Rock wouldn't be complete without dining at Kamat Bugle Rock.
Address:Bull Temple Rd, Basavanagudi, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560004
Timings: 6:00 AM \u2013 8:00 PM

", "blogcontentId": "556"}

{"content": "

ISKCON's gopuram, one of the most modern temple buildings, has complex, traditional woodwork and blue glass. This temple complex, one of the biggest in the world, is devoted to Lord Krishna and Radha. You can admire a gold-plated flag post while strolling beside a lake within. They also provide some of the best-tasting prasadam (holy offerings) in the city.

Evening: 4:15PM-8:00PM
Weekends:7:15PM-8:00PM

", "blogcontentId": "557"}

{"content": "

Architecture lovers especially like the well-known Gavi Gangadhareshwara, a 16th-century building. Lord Shiva rules this place from his natural cave. There are numerous monolithic sculptures scattered across the ancient temple's courtyard. Immense statues of the sun and moon on lofty pillars are another attraction to take in. Sunlight is guaranteed to reach the lingam on Makara Sankranthi through the Nandi's horns because to the temple's construction design.

Timings: 6AM-11:00AM, 5:30PM-8:30PM

", "blogcontentId": "558"}

{"content": "

The Sri Someshwara Temple in Halasuru is another ancient temple that stretches back to the Chola era.It underwent significant renovations when the Vijayanagar Empire was in power. A vibrant gopuram welcomes you at the door. You'll also find beautifully carved pillars within. Additionally, there are other sculptures to be concerned of, such as the one showing the marriage of Lord Shiva and Parvati. And the one in which Mahishasura is defeated by Goddess Durga.
Address: Anugraha Layout, Ramanashree Enclave, Bilekahalli, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560076, India
Timings:  6:00AM-12:30PM, 5:30PM-9:00PM

", "blogcontentId": "559"}

{"content": "

The Hindu deity Jagannath, together with his siblings Subhadra and Balabhadra, are the objects of devotion. Over fifteen thousand worshippers witness the magnificence of this temple annually.
Address: Agara Village, 1st Sector, HSR Layout, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560102
Timings: Monday to Friday: 6:00AM-1:00PM, 4:00PM-9:00 PM Saturday and Sunday: 6:00AM-1:00PM, 3:30PM-9:00PM

", "blogcontentId": "560"}

{"content": "

The construction of Kadu Malleshwara is given to Venkoji, Shivaji's brother. The name Kadu Malleshwara, which means to \"forest,\" comes from the story that during the time it was constructed in the middle of a dense forest. The temple, currently called Kadu Mallikarjunaswamy, is located in the middle of Malleswaram's busy streets. It is well-liked by Shiva enthusiasts and features architecture in the Dravidian style. Move to the Dakshinamukha Nandi Teertha Kalyani Kshetra when you have finished here. It is thought to be approximately four hundred years old and is dedicated to Nandi.
Address: Kadu Malleshwara Temple, Malleshwaram, Bangalore.
Timings: 7:00AM-12:00PM, 5:30PM-8:30PM


", "blogcontentId": "561"}

{"content": "

The Ganesh temple, sometimes called the Shakti Ganapati temple or occasionally the Satya Ganapathy temple, is another temple worth seeing in Bangalore, namely in the Basavanagudi neighborhood. One of the most well-known temples in Bangalore is the huge, over eighteen-foot-tall idol of the god Ganesha, which was made of a single, solid piece of rock. Locals frequently decorate the monument to symbolize many Lord Ganesha incarnations during the Ganesh festival. When the idol is covered in butter weighing at least 100 kg, during the exquisite construction of Benne Alankar, the temple becomes one of the most charming places in Bangalore.
Address:  235, Bull Temple Road, Basavanagudi, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560004
Timings: 6:30 AM to 1:00 PM , 4:30 PM to 8:00 PM

Conclusion

Bangalore preserves its rich history through its many historic temples, even though it is a modern IT city. These temples provide a glimpse into the history of the city, from the vast Nandi statue at the Dodda Basavana Gudi to the beautiful carvings of the Chokkanathaswamy temple.

FAQs

Q.What is the oldest temple in Bangalore?
A.The Chokkanathaswamy temple, dating back to the 10th century CE, is considered one of the oldest temples in Bangalore.
Q.Who built the ISKCON Temple in Bangalore?
A.Part of the global ISKCON initiative, which was initiated to commemorate the birthday of its founder, Sri Prabhupada, was the enormous shrine located in Bangalore. The renowned ISKCON Temple in Bangalore welcomed visitors in May 1997 following its official opening by Mr. Shankar Dayal Sharma, the country's previous president. Thousands of people visit the temple each month.
Q.When is the best time to visit temples in Bangalore?
A.Most of Bangalore's temples are accessible from early in the morning till late at night, with different hours for prayers and rituals. It's important to confirm each temple's specific hours before going.


", "blogcontentId": "562"}
blogs.excerpt: Explore Bangalore’s rich heritage with our guide to 8 iconic temples. Discover their architectural beauty, historical significance, and spiritual charm
blogs.title: 8 Famous Temples In Bangalore

The recent changes in India's tax policy regarding indexation benefits have sent ripples through the high-end real estate market. The government wants simpler taxes. Removing indexation will likely slow property sales. It will especially impact long-term investors. 

Key Takeaways

  • When indexation benefits are removed, it means property owners face higher taxable capital gains. In simpler terms, they end up paying more in taxes. 
  • Impact on High-end real estate investors might feel the pinch more than first-time homebuyers. 
  • Although the long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax rate has been reduced to 12.5%, there\u2019s a twist. The absence of indexation could eat into that benefit. So, it\u2019s not all sunshine and rainbows. 
  • Brace yourself for a slowdown in property sales. Plus, expect more cash transactions. It\u2019s like the real estate market is doing a little shuffle. 
  • Experts have mixed feelings about this new tax regime. Some see it as a red flag for investors.

", "blogcontentId": "544"}

{"content": "

Background on Indexation Benefits

Indexation benefits have been a big help in property transactions in India. They let sellers adjust the price of a property for inflation, which means they pay less tax on their gains. This adjustment uses the Cost Inflation Index (CII), which shows how prices have gone up over time. For years, property owners saved a lot on taxes this way. But now, with a recent announcement by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, things have changed a lot.

How Indexation Works

To understand the impact of removing indexation benefits, it\u2019s essential to grasp how it functions. The formula for calculating the inflation-adjusted purchase price is:
Inflation Adjusted Price = (Original Purchase Price \u00d7 CII of Sale Year / CII of Purchase Year)

This calculation allows property sellers to determine their profits more accurately, reflecting the true economic value of their assets.

Year

CII Value

2001

100

2024

300

For example, if a property was purchased for \u20b910 lakh in 2001, its inflation-adjusted price in 2024 would be \u20b930 lakh, assuming the CII value increased from 100 to 300. This adjustment significantly lowers the taxable capital gains when the property is sold.

", "blogcontentId": "545"}

{"content": "

Recent Policy Changes

These are some of the key points that have come into effect with the announcement of Budget 2024 regarding the sale of a property.
Among the major changes made in the tax regime, some major reliefs and concerns are:

  • Removal of indexation benefits
  • New LTCG tax rate of 12.5%, substantial reduction from the earlier 20%.

However, the effective tax burden may still increase for many sellers since the applicability of indexation has been removed.
This has triggered some debate among real estate experts and investors. According to some, while the step toward a lower tax rate is one positive reform, doing away with indexation benefits would push up taxes for property owners.

Impact on High-End Real Estate

The removal of indexation benefits is particularly concerning for the high-end real estate market. Investors who have held properties for several years may find themselves facing substantial tax liabilities when they decide to sell.

Broader Economic Implications

But the effects of these cuts to indexation benefits are not restricted to the individual property transactions alone. The real estate sector is very essential to the rest of the economy, affecting several sectors such as construction, banking, and home furnishings.

Economic Dynamics

Job Creation: Real estate, when flourishing, will lead to direct and indirect job creation thus, fostering the economy.
Investor Sentiment: The withdrawal of indexation benefits could demotivate and push investors back, which would thereby slowing down the pace of property selling and possibly lead to more cash transactions.
Market Stability: Demand for high-end properties may drop, hence putting a risk on the entire market stability.

Responses from the Real Estate Sector

The real estate sector has responded with mixed feelings to the recent policy changes. While some believe the reduction in LTCG tax is beneficial, the removal of indexation benefits raises concerns.

", "blogcontentId": "546"}

{"content": "

Market Trends and Data

Recent numbers show that the residential real estate market in India has been really thriving, especially after COVID. In 2023, home sales hit their highest levels since 2013, with a 33% increase from the previous year. The first part of 2024 kept this momentum going, with sales jumping by 41%.
With the recent change in indexation benefits, India's fancy real estate market is facing some challenges. Even though the lower LTCG tax rate might look good, it's still unclear how this will affect property sales and how investors feel about it. As the market gets used to these new rules, everyone involved will have to figure out how to deal with this new situation in the real estate world.

", "blogcontentId": "547"}
blogs.excerpt: Discover how removing indexation benefits affects high-end real estate, influencing property values, market trends, and investment strategies
blogs.title: How the Removal of Indexation Benefits Affects High-End Real Estate

Table of Contents

", "blogcontentId": "525"}

{"content": "

Bangalore has a 15% higher cost of living than Pune, mostly because of more rent and transportation expenses. The higher cost of living can be compensated for by Bangalore's generally higher income.

{"content": "

1BHK flats for rent in Bangalore range in monthly rent from \u20b915,000 to \u20b922,000, which is reflective of the city's varied neighborhood offerings and facilities. Bengaluru is a larger, more reputable IT hub with more job opportunities than Pune. But Pune, the country's growing IT and auto manufacturing hub, is fast establishing itself as a serious competitor when it comes to job opportunities. Pune is becoming the new startup hub of India and an attractive choice for people looking for opportunities.

Bangalore may have better transportation and infrastructure than Pune because it has made substantial investments in buses, trains, and metro. Traffic congestion is still a big problem, though. Pune, on the other hand, is said to have less pollution and traffic jams because to its well-established bus and train system.

Bangalore and Delhi, two big Indian cities, often find themselves in a friendly rivalry. In this comprehensive comparison, we delve into various aspects to help you decide which city suits your lifestyle better.

", "blogcontentId": "522"}

{"content": "

Historical Background

Bangalore's history dates back centuries, during which it changed from a small town to a vibrant metropolis. The name \"Garden City\" refers to its formerly plethora of green areas. Delhi has been the capital of several civilizations over its millennia-long history. It represents authority and rule of law as India's political capital at the moment. Bangalore and Delhi have developed different development patterns and cultural features as a result of the different historical influences that have formed their individual identities.

Geographical Features

Located on the Deccan Plateau Bengaluru is well-known for its peaceful and lovely weather. In addition to offering relief from India's hot summers, this mild climate fosters a wide range of parks and green areas that improve the look of the city and promote outdoor sports. Delhi, which is situated in the Indo-Gangetic plains, has severe weather, with hot summers and chilled winters.

Economic Significance

Bangalore's economic significance can be seen by its rapid development as India's Silicon Valley. The lively startup scene in the city makes it an important center for new companies, and its strong IT sector creates a lot of jobs and attracts talent from around the world.
Delhi is the political and administrative core of India and is crucial to the country's economy. Its economic strength is increased by the presence of important government departments, companies, and corporate headquarters here.
Bangalore is a technological powerhouse, with employment available in research, engineering, and software development. Whereas Delhi has a diverse economy that includes jobs in the government, trade, manufacturing etc.

", "blogcontentId": "523"}

{"content": "

Rental Price comparison

Bangalore often has higher rental rates than Delhi. For instance, the average monthly cost of a one-bedroom flat in central Delhi is between INR 10,000 and INR 20,000. As an illustration, the average monthly rent for a 1BHK flat in Bangalore is between INR 15,000 and INR 25,000. In addition, the neighborhood, kind of home, and facilities offered can all affect rental prices.

Traffic and Transportation

Despite efforts to enhance public transit, Bangalore suffers from severe congestion due to the city's rapid urban growth and narrow highways, which make travel times lengthy.
Delhi boasts an advanced transit system with a metro, buses, and suburban trains. Even with the improvements made to public transportation, rush hour traffic bottlenecks still happen in the city.
Bangalore\u2019s public transit improvements are notable but struggle with implementation issues. Delhi\u2019s metro and trains help reduce road traffic, yet challenges remain with environmental impact and last-mile connectivity.

Future Prospects

Bangalore's strong IT industry and its focus on sustainability are expected to fuel the city's continued growth in terms of both population and business.
Delhi remains a significant administrative and business hub, but in order to fit its increasing population, it must address issues like pollution, overcrowding, and inadequate facilities.

Conclusion

Both cities have strong futures: Delhi will combine fresh developments with its rich past, while Bangalore is expected to become an outstanding digital and sustainability metropolis.


", "blogcontentId": "524"}
blogs.excerpt: Discover the ultimate Bangalore vs. Delhi showdown. Compare climate, culture, job opportunities, cost of living, and more to find out which city suits you best.
blogs.title: Bangalore vs. Delhi: The Ultimate Comparison Showdown

Verify that the profile you're using is business-related and not personal. By selecting Settings > Account > Switch to Business Profile, you can change your personal profile to a business profile. {"content": "

{"content": "

For real estate businesses, Instagram Reels are an excellent means to produce interesting content. Use them for giving brief real estate market trends and insights. To give viewers an idea of the neighborhood's special appeal, highlight its landmarks, educational institutions, and infrastructure. Reels on local events, creative home tours, or captivating tales can all add creativity. Entertaining reels, behind-the-scenes glimpses and trendy topics also attract viewers.By providing a variety of content in a single scroll, carousel posts help draw in users by raising interest and engagement. 

", "blogcontentId": "517"}

{"content": "

Using hashtags to connect with individuals who share your interests is a terrific idea. Your postings show up in hashtag search results when you include relevant hashtags. This exposes your material to readers who are interested in the subjects you are posting about but may not be familiar with your brand yet. Each post can include up to 30 hashtags, but try not to use too many. Mix hashtags that are pertinent to the subject of your post with those that are popular. Use hashtags like #realestate #openhouse #househunting #homesforsale, for instance, if you're posting about an open house.

", "blogcontentId": "518"}

{"content": "

Another excellent method for interacting with local leads is geotagging. Your postings show up in the location's feed and search results when you add a location tag to them. Someone searching for \"#Bengalururentalapartments,\" for instance, will see all of the most recent postings about rental apartments in Bengaluru, including yours if you have geotagged it appropriately. When you're attempting to connect with folks in a certain location or neighborhood, geotagging is really helpful.

", "blogcontentId": "519"}
